newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - European ADRs off in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - European ADRs off in New York.

text.p: Most European stocks eased in New York on Wednesday, weighed in part by earnings reports and Britain's decision to increase interest rates, traders said.
American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) for European stocks also were hit by a perception they might have climbed too high, one trader said.

"I think we've had a huge run here; earnings are coming out ... and enthusiasm for that game is running a little thin," he said. "None of these stocks has been helped by Britain's decision to raise rates today" to six from 5.75 percent.
Sweden's Electrolux fell 1-5/8 to 56-1/4 after it reported weak markets in all its European businesses.
Italy's Benetton Group was off one to 23-1/2 and Telefonica de Espana fell 1-3/8 to 60-7/8.
Italy's Elsag Bailey Process Automations NV, controlled by Finmeccanica SpA, closed on Tuesday at 22-5/8 in U.S. trade and its opening was delayed because of an imbalance in bids.
The stock was indicated to open between 15-1/4 and 16-1/2 after Merrill Lynch, Alex. Brown and McDonald & Co cut the company's ratings. The company's 12-month low is 19-5/8.

British Airways was up two to 91 after the British government said it would resume "open skies" trade talks with the United States next week. The carrier is seeking to join forces with AMR Corp's American Airlines in the trans-Atlantic market.
Britain's Vodafone Group Plc rose 1/2 to 38-3/8 on market talk AT&T Corp planned to bid for it. Vodafone declined comment on the rumors.
Latin American stocks were largely quiet, with investors focusing on U.S. economic data. Brazil's Telebras was off 1/2 to 73-3/4.

Among Israeli stocks, Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd was up 1-1/2 to 41. The company said on Tuesday it had gotten approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to make and market its Nicardipine calcium channel blockers.
In an index of 441 selected ADRs declining and advancing stocks were tied at 134 in late morning. Volume was 19.1 million shares.
